name: Sukarno
summary: Indonesian nationalist leader and first president, who framed his politics as anti-imperialist nationalism combined with internationalism, democracy by deliberation and consensus, social justice and belief in God (Pancha Shila). He rejected both the liberal and the communist model and led the non-aligned movement. This local-phase draft rests on his 1960 UN speech only.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Led the national revolution that fought the Dutch after 1945 until transfer of sovereignty in 1949.

arms-reduction.rationale: Built up his forces with about a billion dollars of Soviet arms rather than keep them to a minimum.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banned Masyumi and the PSI in August 1960, citing their part in the PRRI insurrection and refusal to recognise Guided Democracy.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: When the assembly rejected the government's budget in 1960 he replaced it with a nominated provisional parliament.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Led the revolution against Dutch colonial rule and spent years in jail and exile for challenging it.

close-ties-china.rationale: After 1958 he grew closer to the Soviet Union and especially the People's Republic of China, while breaking with the United States by 1963.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Spent two years in Dutch jail and eight in exile for challenging colonialism, then led the revolution that ended Dutch rule.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The elected Constituent Assembly deadlocked and he dissolved it in 1959, imposing the 1945 constitution by decree.

defeat-communism.rationale: Protected the PKI against army moves, banned movements opposing it, promoted its leaders and built Nasakom around communist participation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Insists on strict equality of sovereignty and says no nation can be made to surrender any part of it except freely and equally (paras 48-52).

democracy-best.rationale: After the 1955 elections he dismantled parliamentary democracy and replaced it with Guided Democracy, which Britannica calls dictatorship in substance.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Dismantled the multiparty parliament to 'bury' feuding parties, banned Masyumi and the PSI and put appointed functional groups in the legislature.

elective-rulers.rationale: Became Lifetime President as an official title under the appointed assembly rather than by popular election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Proclaimed martial law on 14 March 1957 to end the liberal phase while regional rebellions spread.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: His government crushed the South Maluku republic in 1950 and the PRRI/Permesta rebellion of 1958 by military action.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: His government ran an aggressive foreign policy against the new state of Malaysia, which he called an imperialist plot, and quit the UN over it.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: Dissolved the House by decree in 1959 and replaced the budget-rejecting assembly with a nominated one in 1960.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Seized Dutch enterprises in 1957 and justified the economic cost as integral to making independence real for Indonesians.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Says any transgression against one nation's sovereignty threatens all, and that the great powers have no right to settle the world's future (paras 52, 56).

land-redistribution.rationale: Called for implementation of the 1960 land reform laws, under which land was taken from landlords and given to poor peasants.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Backed a unitary secular state that collided with Muslim demands, and his government executed the Darul Islam leader who sought a Muslim theocracy.

leader-cult.rationale: Accepted acclamation as Great Leader of the Revolution and, as his official title, Lifetime President, with crowds chanting his slogans.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Replaced free enterprise with a Guided Economy after dismantling the parliamentary system.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Pursued military confrontation against the Dutch over West New Guinea and vowed to crush Malaysia.

military-superiority.rationale: Obtained about a billion dollars of Soviet arms while pursuing campaigns over West New Guinea and Malaysia.

more-religion-public.rationale: Places belief in God at the forefront of the state's philosophy and its political, economic and social activity (paras 129, 140).

nation-first.rationale: Presents internationalism as the third pillar, consistent with nationalism, and criticises members who use the UN for narrow national advantage (paras 135, 152).

national-resource-control.rationale: Nationalised Dutch-owned firms including the oil company and put control of oil in the new state company Permina.

national-self-determination.rationale: Says the struggle for independence is always justified and just, and that nationalism is the spring of liberty for every nation (paras 64, 131).

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Says Indonesia follows neither the liberal nor the communist conception and has built its own synthesis, Pancha Shila, while admiring both (paras 122-124).

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Took several wives in the decades after his first marriages, practising polygamy as a Muslim.

organic-representation.rationale: Gave 154 of 238 seats in the 1960 legislature to appointed functional groups, including the military, in place of party-based election.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Dissolved the elected House of Representatives by decree in July 1959 and put an appointed legislature in its place.

party-controls-media.rationale: His government jailed the editor of the critical paper Indonesia Raya without trial and shut the paper in 1958.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Holds that decisions should come from deliberation (musjawarah) toward unanimity (mufakat), with no voting contest or taking of sides, for Indonesia and for the UN (paras 153-156).

public-ownership.rationale: The seizure of Dutch firms in 1957 (shipping, Shell) and the Guided Economy put major industries under the state, which he defended as integral to independence.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resisted the IMF and United States push for rational economic policy and rejected American aid in 1963.

religious-nation.rationale: Describes the nation as plural in religion, with belief in God as a shared principle that even non-believers accept, not one religion defining it (para 129).

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Declared independence in 1945 and led a revolution against the Dutch.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Says international social justice means a united effort to help underdeveloped nations, with aid free of the cold war and funded by disarmament (paras 86, 170).

right-to-secede.rationale: Suppressed the South Maluku republic and the PRRI/Permesta regional rebellion rather than let regions leave.

separated-powers.rationale: Dissolved the elected House in 1959, appointed the replacement legislatures and replaced the assembly that rejected his budget, ending checks on the presidency.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ran a Guided Economy and an eight-year state plan after nationalising Dutch enterprises.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Makes belief in God the first pillar of the state, so state promotion of atheism contradicts it (paras 128-129, 140).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Hosted the 1955 Bandung conference, led a neutralist foreign policy and joined no military bloc.

strong-leader.rationale: Dissolved the elected House by decree in 1959, restored the strong-presidency 1945 constitution and ruled through Guided Democracy over a parliament he had replaced.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Fukuyama reports that after 1957 martial law Sukarno, backed by the army and the Communists, crushed the liberal opposition while keeping Nasakom parties inside his National Front.

term-limits.rationale: Took the title Lifetime President instead of leaving office after any set number of terms.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pursued the Greater Indonesia policy and aggressive campaigns over West New Guinea and the new Malaysia.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Calls Pancha Shila the essence of two thousand years of Indonesian civilization and speaks of centuries of strong nationhood before imperialism (paras 126-127).

universal-morality.rationale: Treats the Declaration of Independence's words as universal in time and place, and Pancha Shila as universally applicable (paras 46, 141).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Held office as Lifetime President, with no limit on his tenure.

notes: Local and web phases. Record sources added in the web phase: Britannica (biography, Sukarno's policies), the Library of Congress country study and a PEN case file. Record answers replace the earlier words-only answers where a record exists; the rest stay on his 1960 UN speech. Themes searched: government (parliament, parties, media, emergency rule), economy (nationalisation, land reform, aid), world (Malaysia, West New Guinea, blocs, UN), society (religion, family). His own books, 1945 and Bandung speeches could not be obtained in full text; see notFound.
